mainTopic: רבא's rule on salting with forbidden food, שמואל's laws of salting meat, and the משניות on בשר בחלב
overview: The amud opens by asking why רבא needed his own source to forbid kosher meat salted with טריפה meat, when שמואל already taught that salted food is like boiling food. The answer is that שמואל's rule might cover only blood, while רבא teaches that juices and gravy also forbid. The גמרא then tests רבא against a ברייתא about a kosher fish salted with a non-kosher fish, and each challenge is answered by reading the ברייתא's wording carefully. Next comes a memory sign for three teachings of שמואל: meat must be salted and rinsed well, salted meat must sit on a vessel with holes, and breaking an animal's neck before it dies traps blood in the meat. Along the way the גמרא adds the order of rinsing and salting, which inner parts are not assumed to have blood, and that several pieces may be salted together. The question of whether neck-broken meat is forbidden even for the owner ends in תיקו. A new משנה teaches that putting chicken and cheese on one table breaks no Torah law, since עוף in milk is only rabbinic. Another משנה sets out which meat and milk fall under בשר בחלב, with the views of רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי. The גמרא then begins looking for the source, with רבי אלעזר's proof from 'the kid of the goats' continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not just quote שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed his own source when שמואל already taught that salted food is like boiling food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let רבא say his ruling based on שמואל, because שמואל said: salted food is like boiling food, and pickled food is like cooked food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's method. It asks why he didn't just rely on שמואל's well-known rule to forbid the kosher meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that salting makes food pass taste the way boiling does. If so, kosher meat salted with טריפה meat would already be forbidden. So why did רבא need a separate source? The question is about method, not about the ruling itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Boiling hot food, which passes and absorbs taste

phrases.english: But let him say it from Shmuel's statement,
phrases.notes: The גמרא means רבא should have given his ruling using שמואל's rule.

phrases.english: as Shmuel said:
Salted food is like boiling food,
and pickled food is like cooked food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source behind רבא's ruling from earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice of source for forbidding kosher meat salted with טריפה meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's rule already makes salted food pass taste like boiling food, so רבא's own source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: שמואל's rule may cover only blood
steps.stepSummary: From שמואל alone we might think only blood is passed by salting, not juices and gravy, so רבא's teaching is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had שמואל, I would have said: this applies only to their blood, but not to their juices and gravy. So רבא's teaching tells us that juices and gravy also count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's rule alone would leave a gap. רבא's teaching fills that gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have limited שמואל's rule to blood. During salting, the blood drips out and is not absorbed by the other piece, so the kosher meat might seem fine. רבא's teaching shows that the juices and gravy of the טריפה meat can also make the kosher meat forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought, meaning the mistaken first assumption
The juice that comes out of meat or fish
Gravy, the fatty liquid of the meat

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule could have been limited to blood. רבא teaches that the juices and gravy of the טריפה meat also forbid the kosher meat during salting.

phrases.english: If it were from Shmuel, I would have said:
this applies only to their blood,
but their juices and gravy, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: This is רבא's teaching, which shows that juices and gravy count too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that רבא's source adds something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From שמואל we might think salting passes only blood, not juices and gravy.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's teaching shows that juices and gravy also forbid the kosher meat.

steps.title: Challenge from a kosher fish salted with a non-kosher fish
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits a kosher fish salted with a non-kosher fish, which seems to show that juices do not forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a kosher fish that someone salted with a non-kosher fish is permitted. Isn't this talking about a case where both fish were salted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבא. It suggests that the ברייתא is talking about a case where both fish were salted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both fish were salted, the non-kosher fish would give off juice. Yet the ברייתא still permits the kosher fish. That would mean juices do not forbid, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? A way of suggesting how to read a source

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: דָּג טָהוֹר שֶׁמְּלָחוֹ עִם דָּג טָמֵא – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: A kosher fish that one salted with a non-kosher fish is permitted.
Is it not where both of them were salted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 2 that juices forbid.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the juices of forbidden food make food salted with it forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both fish were salted, the non-kosher juice would pass into the kosher fish, yet the ברייתא permits it.

steps.title: Only the kosher fish was salted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of a case where the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher fish was unsalted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher fish was unsalted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as a different case. Only the kosher fish was salted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unsalted fish gives off no juice, so nothing forbidden passes into the kosher fish. That is why the kosher fish stays permitted, and רבא's rule is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as a case where...

phrases.english: No, it is a case where the kosher fish was salted
and the non-kosher fish was unsalted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה טָהוֹר מָלִיחַ וְטָמֵא תָּפֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about both fish being salted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the kosher fish was salted, so no non-kosher juice came out.

steps.title: The second clause shows the first clause means both salted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's second clause lists the case of salted kosher and unsalted non-kosher separately, so the first clause must be about both salted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause teaches: 'but if the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher was unsalted,' we can learn that the first clause is dealing with a case where both are salted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4. It points to the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא opens with 'but' and then names the case of salted kosher and unsalted non-kosher. That suggests the רישא is a different case, meaning both fish were salted. If so, the first challenge to רבא comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a ברייתא or משנה
By implication, we can learn from this

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: the case in the סיפא is exactly the case the גמרא just used to explain the רישא. That overlap is the whole problem being raised.

phrases.english: But since the last clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה טָהוֹר מָלִיחַ וְטָמֵא תָּפֵל,
phrases.english: 'But if the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher one unsalted,'
it follows that in the first clause
we are dealing with a case where both are salted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 4 based on the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 4 that the רישא speaks of only the kosher fish being salted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא states this exact case separately, so the רישא must be about both fish being salted.

steps.title: The second clause explains the first
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is not a new case. It explains how the רישא should be understood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining: a kosher fish that one salted with a non-kosher fish is permitted. How so? When the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher fish was unsalted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second clause explains the first clause. It is not a separate case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the ברייתא as a rule followed by 'how so?' The kosher fish is permitted only when the non-kosher fish was unsalted. So the ברייתא never permits a case where both fish were salted, and רבא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining, meaning the later clause explains the earlier one

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא permits the kosher fish only when the non-kosher fish was unsalted and gave off no juice. This fits רבא's rule that juices passed during salting forbid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads a ברייתא: a later clause can explain an earlier one instead of adding a new case.

phrases.english: It is explaining:

phrases.aramaic: טָהוֹר שֶׁמְּלָחוֹ עִם דָּג טָמֵא – מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: a kosher fish that one salted with a non-kosher fish is permitted.
How so?
When the kosher fish was salted and the non-kosher one unsalted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and confirms the reading of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא: the סיפא explains the רישא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is a separate case, so the רישא must mean both fish were salted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא explains the רישא: the kosher fish is permitted only when the non-kosher fish was unsalted.

steps.title: Logic supports reading the first clause as kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer of step 6. If the רישא meant 'both salted' and still permitted, there would be no need for the סיפא to teach the easier case of 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense this way. If you think the first clause is about both fish salted, then once we know 'both salted' is permitted, do we really need to be told that 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted' is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a logical support for the answer it just gave. The סיפא only makes sense as an explanation, because if the רישא were 'both salted,' the סיפא would add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted' is an easier case than 'both salted,' because the non-kosher fish has no salt pulling its juices out. A ברייתא does not bother teaching an easier case after a harder one. So the רישא must not be 'both salted,' and the סיפא is just explaining it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable; it makes sense
It enters your mind; if you would think
Here: a kosher fish / a non-kosher fish
Is it necessary to say? Used when a case is obvious from another case

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
phrases.notes: He means the answer from the last step, that the סיפא only explains the רישא.

phrases.english: for if it would enter your mind
that the first clause is where both are salted,
now, if both salted is permitted,
is it necessary to teach kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings logical support for the answer of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא explains the רישא, so the רישא is 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted' and not 'both salted.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a ברייתא does not teach an easier case after a harder one (the מיבעיא logic).

steps.title: The support is rejected: the second clause can be there to reveal the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support. The רישא could really mean 'both salted.' The סיפא was added so we would not mistakenly read the רישא as only 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is your reason, it proves nothing. The second clause was taught to show us what the first clause means. Without it, you might say the first clause is only kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted, but both salted is forbidden. So it taught the second clause as 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted,' which shows that the first clause is about both salted, and even so it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the support from step 7. It shows another reason the ברייתא would include the סיפא even if the רישא is 'both salted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is not adding an easy case. Its job could be to clarify the רישא: by writing 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted' separately, it would show that the רישא is a different case, 'both salted,' and that case is permitted. This only knocks down the support from step 7. The reading of step 6 is still possible, so רבא is not refuted, and the next step brings a new challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: It is no proof; that reasoning does not hold
To reveal; to show the meaning of
By implication; from this we learn

steps.confusionAlert: Both step 6 and this step say the סיפא 'explains' the רישא, but in opposite directions. Step 6 says the סיפא explains that the רישא is 'kosher salted, non-kosher unsalted.' Here the סיפא shows that the רישא is a different case, 'both salted.'

phrases.english: If it is because of this, it is no proof,
he taught the latter clause to reveal the first clause,
so that you should not say the first clause is
kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted,
but if both are salted it is forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא סֵיפָא טָהוֹר מָלִיחַ וְטָמֵא תָּפֵל,
phrases.english: so he taught the latter clause: kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted,
which implies that the first clause is both salted,
and even so it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical support brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the support of step 7 only. It does not settle the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מיבעיא logic ignores that the סיפא may be there to clarify the רישא, not to add a new easy case.

steps.title: A challenge to רבא from the last clause of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The last clause forbids 'non-kosher salted, kosher unsalted.' This implies that 'both salted' is permitted, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the last part of the last clause: but if the non-kosher fish was salted and the kosher fish unsalted, it is forbidden. So only non-kosher salted with kosher unsalted is forbidden, but if both are salted, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבא from the third clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clause names only one forbidden case: the non-kosher fish salted and the kosher fish unsalted. The inference is that any other case, including 'both salted,' is permitted. That goes against רבא, who holds that juices pass during salting and forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the end; the last clause of the ברייתא
But (implied); introduces what we learn from the wording

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter part of the latter clause:
But if the non-kosher fish was salted
and the kosher fish unsalted, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: טָמֵא מָלִיחַ וְטָהוֹר תָּפֵל הוּא דְּאָסוּר,
phrases.english: Only non-kosher salted and kosher unsalted is forbidden,
but if both are salted, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a different clause of the same ברייתא to challenge רבא again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's teaching that juices pass through salting and forbid the kosher fish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The clause forbids only 'non-kosher salted, kosher unsalted,' which implies 'both salted' is permitted.

steps.title: The last clause was only worded to match the clause before it
steps.stepSummary: The last clause says 'non-kosher salted, kosher unsalted' only to match the wording of the clause before it. Nothing can be learned from it about 'both salted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the earlier clause said 'kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted,' the last clause also said 'non-kosher salted and kosher unsalted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9. The wording of the last clause was chosen for style, to match the clause before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wrote its clauses as a matching pair. Because the wording comes from matching, we cannot draw an inference from it that 'both salted' is permitted. So רבא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it taught; the wording was chosen to match an earlier clause

steps.whatToRemember: None of the clauses of the ברייתא disproves רבא. The answer each time is about how to read the ברייתא's wording. רבא's rule, that salting moves juices and gravy, stands.

phrases.english: Since he taught in the earlier clause:
phrases.notes: Here 'רישא' means the clause just before this one, the middle clause of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: kosher salted and non-kosher unsalted,
he also taught in the last clause:
non-kosher salted and kosher unsalted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording was chosen to match the clause before it (אגב).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The specific wording of the last clause implies that 'both salted' is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording only matches the clause before it, so nothing can be learned about 'both salted.' רבא stands.

steps.title: A memory sign for שמואל's teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short סימן to help remember a set of שמואל's teachings that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: meat, that is placed, departing.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory sign before a new section. This line sets up the teachings that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one of שמואל's teachings. 'Meat' points to his rule about getting the blood out of meat. 'That is placed' points to his rule about where salted meat is put. 'Departing' points to a teaching that comes later on the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign, a short phrase that helps you remember a list of teachings

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a ruling. It is only a memory aid.

phrases.english: (A memory sign:
meat, that is placed, departing.)
phrases.notes: These words are a memory aid for שמואל's rules: 'meat' comes right below, 'that is placed' a bit later, and 'departing' after that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of רבא's view in steps 9-10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. A memory sign for the upcoming teachings of שמואל.

steps.title: Meat must be salted well and rinsed well
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that meat only loses its blood if it is salted very well and rinsed very well.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Meat does not get rid of its blood unless a person salts it very well and rinses it very well.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the basic rule for taking the blood out of meat. You need two things: good salting and good rinsing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salt pulls the blood out of the meat. The rinsing washes off the salt and the blood that came out. 'Very well' is said twice to show that a quick, light job is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From the status of its blood, meaning rid of its forbidden blood

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the הלכה that meat must be salted and rinsed before it may be eaten.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Meat does not become free of its blood,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה,
phrases.english: unless one salts it very thoroughly,
and rinses it very thoroughly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הַבָּשָׂר יוֹצֵא מִידֵי דָּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first teaching hinted at by 'meat' in the memory sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat is only free of its blood if it is salted thoroughly and rinsed thoroughly.

steps.title: Two different orders: salt-rinse or rinse-salt-rinse
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says to salt and then rinse. A ברייתא says to rinse, then salt, then rinse again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב הונא says: One salts and then rinses. A ברייתא taught: One rinses, salts, and rinses again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two sources about the order of salting and rinsing. They seem to disagree, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא lists only two actions: salt, then rinse. The ברייתא adds a rinse before the salting too. So the question is whether a first rinse is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna said:
One salts and rinses.
In a baraita it was taught:
One rinses, and salts, and rinses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: מוֹלֵחַ וּמֵדִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details on the order of salting and rinsing that שמואל mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: salt, then rinse. ברייתא: rinse, salt, then rinse.

steps.title: Both are right, depending on the butcher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two sources do not argue. If the butcher already washed the meat, salt-then-rinse is enough. If not, you must rinse first too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This one (רב הונא) is where the meat was washed at the butcher. That one (the ברייתא) is where it was not washed at the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent argument from step 13. Each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rinse is needed before salting. If the butcher already washed the meat, that counts as the first rinse, so רב הונא only lists salt and rinse. If the butcher did not wash it, you must do the first rinse yourself, as the ברייתא says.
steps.whatToRemember: Meat needs a rinse before salting and a rinse after. If the butcher already washed it, that first rinse is done.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this is where it was washed at the butcher's,
phrases.notes: 'This' is רב הונא's rule of only salt and rinse.

phrases.english: that is where it was not washed at the butcher's.
phrases.notes: 'That' is the ברייתא, which adds a rinse before salting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent conflict between רב הונא and the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רב הונא and the ברייתא argue about whether a rinse before salting is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree a first rinse is needed; רב הונא speaks where the butcher already washed the meat.

steps.title: How רב דימי salted his meat
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי from נהרדעא would salt meat with coarse salt and then shake the salt off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא would salt the meat with coarse salt and then shake it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what one sage actually did when salting meat. It shows a practical way of salting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He used coarse salt, with big grains. After the salt did its work, he shook the salt off the meat.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a
would salt it with coarse salt,
and shake it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא מָלַח לֵיהּ בְּמִילְחָא גְּלָלְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical example of how salting was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב דימי salted with coarse salt and then shook it off.

steps.title: No assumption of blood in the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא rules that we do not assume there is blood in the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: We do not assume there is blood in the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא gives a new rule about the inner parts of the animal. We do not treat the intestines as having blood that must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular meat has blood inside that must be drawn out by salting. The intestines are different, so we do not presume blood is in them. This is a special outcome for these parts, not a change to the basic salting rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not presume, we do not assume

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
We do not presume blood in the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: אֵין מַחֲזִיקִין דָּם בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to salt meat to which parts are not assumed to have blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not assume there is blood in the intestines.

steps.title: Which intestines רב משרשיא meant
steps.stepSummary: The Sages explained that רב משרשיא's rule refers to the rectum, the intestines, and the spiral colon.
steps.simpleTranslation: They explained it as referring to the rectum, the intestines, and the spiral colon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which parts רב משרשיא was talking about. It narrows his rule to three parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Intestines' could be a broad word. The גמרא limits it to three specific parts of the digestive tract.

keyTerms.meaning: The spiral colon, the part that winds around

phrases.english: They explained it as referring to the rectum,
the intestines, and the spiral colon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the parts included in רב משרשיא's rule from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב משרשיא's rule applies to the rectum, the intestines, and the spiral colon.

steps.title: Salted meat goes only on a vessel with holes
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that salted meat may be put only on a vessel with holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: We place salted meat only on a vessel that has holes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the second rule from the memory sign ('that is placed'). Salted meat must sit on something with holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salt draws blood out of the meat. A vessel with holes lets that blood drain away. Without holes, the blood would sit around the meat.
steps.whatToRemember: Meat must be rinsed, salted well, and rinsed again, and while salting it must sit on something with holes so the blood drains.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for salting meat on a rack or board that lets the blood run off.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One does not place salted meat
except on a perforated vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין מַנִּיחִין בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to שמואל's teachings, matching 'that is placed' in the memory sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat may be placed only on a perforated vessel.

steps.title: רב ששת salted meat one piece at a time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב ששת salted his meat piece by piece, never two pieces together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would salt meat one piece at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רב ששת salted his meat: one piece at a time. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a report of a practice, not a stated rule. Because it looks like an extra stringency, the גמרא will want to know the reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: He salted (meat, to draw out the blood)
Literally 'bone by bone'; here it means piece by piece

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would salt it
bone by bone.
phrases.notes: 'Bone' here just means a piece of meat. He salted one piece at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מָלַח לֵיהּ גַּרְמָא גַּרְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of how to salt meat, adding another sage's practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת salted each piece of meat separately.

steps.title: Why not salt two pieces together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ששת avoided salting two pieces together. It suggests that blood leaving one piece might soak into the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would he not salt two pieces together? Is it because blood leaves this piece and that piece soaks it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב ששת's practice and offers a possible answer. The next step will test that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested worry is that blood pushed out of one piece could be absorbed by a piece lying next to it. If that were true, salting several pieces together would be a problem.

phrases.english: Two, what is the reason not?
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't he salt two pieces at once?

phrases.english: Because blood leaves this one
and that one absorbs it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the practice reported in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רב ששת would not salt two pieces together.

steps.title: The same worry would apply to one piece
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested reason: one single piece also lets blood out of one side, and the other side could soak it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even one piece should be a problem. Blood leaves this side of it and that side absorbs it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reason it just suggested. That reason would make salting even a single piece impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If blood leaving one piece could soak into another, the same thing could happen inside one piece, from one side to the other. Since we certainly salt single pieces, the suggested worry cannot be correct.

phrases.english: With one as well, it leaves this side
and that side absorbs it!

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד נָמֵי פָּרֵישׁ מֵהַאי גִּיסָא וּבָלַע הַאי גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason suggested in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed reason that blood moves from one piece into another.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same logic would forbid salting even one piece, which is clearly allowed.

steps.title: No difference between one piece and many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that salting one piece and salting several pieces together are the same. Both are fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that there is no real difference, so you may salt several pieces together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason offered to forbid salting pieces together failed, so the גמרא treats one piece and many pieces the same way. רב ששת's habit is not taken as a binding rule.
steps.whatToRemember: You may salt several pieces of meat together. It is no worse than salting one piece.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the rejection in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Salting many pieces together is the same as salting one, and it is allowed.

steps.title: Breaking an animal's neck before it dies
steps.stepSummary: שמואל quotes רבי חייא: breaking an animal's neck after שחיטה but before it dies makes the meat heavy, cheats people, and traps blood in the limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא: One who breaks an animal's neck before its life leaves it makes the meat heavier, robs people, and causes blood to be absorbed in the limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new teaching from רבי חייא. Breaking the neck too early traps blood in the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the blood drains out when the animal dies. Breaking the neck early keeps blood inside, so the meat weighs more. Customers who buy by weight end up paying for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Before its life leaves it (before it fully dies)

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
One who breaks the neck of an animal
before its life departs,
phrases.notes: This is after the animal was slaughtered, while it is still dying.

phrases.english: this one makes the meat heavy,
and robs people,
and causes blood to be absorbed in the limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא: הַשּׁוֹבֵר מַפְרַקְתָּהּ שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third teaching of שמואל hinted at by 'departing' (נפקותא) in the memory sign of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking the neck before death traps blood, adds weight, and cheats buyers.

steps.title: Is the meat forbidden even for oneself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read שמואל's words. Is the only problem cheating customers, so it is fine for oneself? Or is the trapped blood also a reason the meat is forbidden even for oneself?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: How is he speaking? Does he mean he makes the meat heavy and robs people because he traps blood in the limbs, so for himself it is fine? Or perhaps it is forbidden even for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to read שמואל's statement. Does the trapped blood only matter because it cheats buyers, or does it also make the meat forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: 'traps blood' only explains why the meat is heavier, so the problem is robbery alone. Reading two: 'traps blood' is a separate problem, the blood itself, so the meat is forbidden even if he keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)
How is he saying it? (How should his words be read?)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: How is he saying it?

phrases.aramaic: מַכְבִּיד אֶת הַבָּשָׂר, וְגוֹזֵל אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת
phrases.english: He makes the meat heavy and robs people
because he causes blood to be absorbed in the limbs,
phrases.notes: In this reading, the trapped blood is only the reason the meat is heavier.

phrases.english: so for himself it is fine,
or perhaps for himself it is also forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the statement in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the trapped blood makes the meat forbidden, or only creates a problem of cheating buyers.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stands without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two readings, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. We do not know whether the meat is forbidden for the owner himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question remains unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: It is clear that breaking the neck early cheats buyers. Whether the meat is also forbidden to the owner remains a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 24 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question is unresolved: it is unknown whether the meat is forbidden even for oneself.

steps.title: New משנה: chicken and cheese on the table
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that someone who puts poultry together with cheese on his table does not break a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who places poultry with cheese on the table does not violate a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה. Putting chicken and cheese on the same table is not a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks only about placing the foods on the table, not eating them together. It says no Torah לאו is broken by doing this.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה only says no Torah prohibition is broken. It does not say this is fully allowed in every way.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who brings up poultry with cheese
onto the table,
does not violate a negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּעֲלֶה אֶת הָעוֹף עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic, meat and milk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing poultry with cheese on the table is not a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: Does the משנה imply chicken with milk is a Torah prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's wording precisely. It says putting chicken and cheese on the table breaks no Torah prohibition. That suggests eating them together would break one, and this goes against רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says only that putting them on the table is not a Torah prohibition. That implies that eating them together does break a Torah prohibition. So learn from here that poultry in milk is forbidden by Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a careful inference from the משנה in Step 26 and finds that it seems to make chicken with milk a Torah-level prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stressed only the case of placing chicken and cheese on a table. Pointing out only that case suggests that eating is different and is a real לא תעשה. That would clash with רבי עקיבא, who holds that עוף in milk is not forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (an inference drawn from a text)

phrases.english: GEMARA
But if he eats it, he violates a Torah prohibition,
learn from this:
poultry meat in milk is forbidden by Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה quoted in Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי עקיבא that עוף in milk is not a Torah prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the משנה limits its statement to placing the foods on the table, it implies that eating them is a Torah violation.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as: placing them together will not lead to a Torah sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. Putting chicken and cheese on the table does not lead a person to a Torah prohibition, because even eating them together is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: one who puts poultry with cheese on the table will not come to a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the משנה seemed to mean 'placing them is not a Torah sin, but eating them is.' Now it means 'placing them cannot lead to a Torah sin at all,' because even if he eats them, the prohibition is only rabbinic. This fits רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the law. It is only showing that the משנה's words can mean 'will not lead to a Torah sin,' which does not imply that eating is a Torah sin.

phrases.english: Say:
one who places the poultry with the cheese
on the table
does not come to a Torah prohibition.
phrases.notes: Even if he ends up eating them together, that is only rabbinic, so placing them can never lead to a Torah sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא הַמַּעֲלֶה אֶת הָעוֹף עִם הַגְּבִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implied that eating chicken with cheese is a Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that placing them together cannot lead to any Torah prohibition, which fits רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Chicken with cheese is a rabbinic prohibition. The משנה's wording fits this once it is read correctly.

steps.title: New משנה: which meat and which milk are included
steps.stepSummary: Kosher meat in milk from any kosher animal may not be cooked and gives no benefit. If either the meat or the milk comes from a non-kosher animal, both cooking and benefit are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat of a kosher animal in milk of a kosher animal may not be cooked, and benefit from it is forbidden. Meat of a kosher animal in milk of a non-kosher animal, or meat of a non-kosher animal in milk of a kosher animal, may be cooked, and benefit from it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה sets out the basic rule of which animals' meat and milk fall under בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'a kid in its mother's milk,' but the משנה teaches that any kosher animal's milk counts, not only the mother's. Both the meat and the milk must come from kosher animals. If either one is non-kosher, the Torah prohibition does not apply at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher domesticated animal (cow, sheep, goat)
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: MISHNA
Meat of a kosher animal
in milk of a kosher animal
is forbidden to cook and forbidden for benefit.
Meat of a kosher animal
in milk of a non-kosher animal,
meat of a non-kosher animal
in milk of a kosher animal
is permitted to cook and permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּשַׂר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בַּחֲלֵב בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בשר בחלב applies only when both the meat and the milk come from kosher animals, and then cooking and benefit are both forbidden.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: three verses exclude חיה, עוף, and a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says חיה and עוף in milk are not forbidden by the Torah. The Torah repeats 'a kid in its mother's milk' three times, and each time excludes one category.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: undomesticated animals and birds are not forbidden by the Torah. It says 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk' three times, to exclude a חיה, a bird, and a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with רבי עקיבא's view and his source from the three repetitions of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'kid' (גדי) points to a kosher בהמה. The three repetitions are read as three exclusions: חיה, עוף, and בהמה טמאה. So חיה and עוף in milk are not forbidden by the Torah, and a non-kosher animal is not included at all, as the משנה already said it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An undomesticated kosher animal (like a deer)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
an undomesticated animal and a bird are not forbidden by Torah law,
as it says, 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk'
three times
to exclude an undomesticated animal, a bird, and a non-kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר חַיָּה וָעוֹף אֵינָם מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with רבי עקיבא's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חיה, עוף, and בהמה טמאה in milk are not forbidden by the Torah.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the link to נבלה, and why עוף is still excluded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי links בשר בחלב to the נבלה prohibition in the same פסוק. Anything that becomes forbidden as נבלה is included. עוף is left out because a bird has no mother's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: It says 'Do not eat any carcass,' and it says 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.' What is forbidden as a נבלה is forbidden to cook in milk. A bird is forbidden as a נבלה, so I might think it is forbidden to cook in milk. The verse says 'in its mother's milk,' which leaves out a bird, since it has no mother's milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי הגלילי's different way of learning the law. It starts with a broad rule and then narrows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two prohibitions sit side by side in the פסוק, whatever can become נבלה is included. That would include חיה and even עוף. The words 'its mother's milk' then remove עוף, since birds do not nurse. On his view, חיה remains included by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The verse teaches (to correct that thought)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי הגלילי excludes only עוף. Unlike רבי עקיבא, he holds that חיה is included by Torah law, since it can become נבלה and it does have mother's milk.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
it says, 'You shall not eat any carcass,'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21. It is the same פסוק that also says not to cook a kid in milk.

phrases.english: and it says, 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk,'
what is forbidden because of נבלה
is forbidden to cook in milk.
A bird, which is forbidden because of נבלה,
one might think it is forbidden to cook in milk?
The verse teaches, 'in its mother's milk':

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא עוֹף שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֲלֵב אֵם.
phrases.english: this excludes a bird, which has no mother's milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר נֶאֱמַר לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כׇל נְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view, different from רבי עקיבא's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever can become נבלה is included in בשר בחלב, except עוף, which has no mother's milk.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא excludes חיה and עוף from the Torah law. רבי יוסי הגלילי excludes only עוף.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's first rule comes from: that the law covers all kosher animals and any kosher milk, not only a real kid goat in its own mother's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these things known?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking for the source of its opening rule. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק literally says 'a kid in its mother's milk.' The משנה, however, forbids any kosher animal's meat in any kosher animal's milk. The גמרא wants to know how the words of the פסוק cover so much more.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה in Step 29
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that בשר בחלב is not limited to an actual kid goat in its own mother's milk

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins: the פסוק about יהודה sending 'the kid of the goats'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points to the story of יהודה, where the Torah writes 'kid of the goats.' The fact that the Torah adds 'of the goats' there suggests that the plain word 'kid' can mean the young of other animals too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The verse says, 'And Judah sent the kid of the goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts to answer the question by bringing a פסוק from the story of יהודה. The proof continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There, the Torah needed to say 'of the goats' to make clear it meant a goat. That implies the word גדי alone is broader and can include the young of a cow or sheep. So 'a kid' in the בשר בחלב verse is not limited to goats.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The verse states:
'And Judah sent the kid of the goats,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:20. Notice the extra words 'of the goats.' The proof depends on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר קְרָא וַיִּשְׁלַח יְהוּדָה אֶת גְּדִי הָעִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a word-usage proof from the פסוק about יהודה, showing that גדי alone can mean the young of other animals. The argument continues after this point.
